chapter: Writing, Oklahoma roots and the origins of bebop
title: Frank Wess and the Oklahoma sound
summary: Gitler asks about the Royals and Wess, and the Southwest style.

story.theme_name: Playing with Count Basie: joining, leading, leaving
story.community_name: Playing with Count Basie: the band, its feel and its people

blocks.x: You had mentioned earlier, when we were talking, about knowing the Royal brothers in Oklahoma.
Oh yeah, but that was way back.
But that's where I'm really concentrating now. And you said Frank Wess, too.
Yeah, Frank Wess was there. He was from Sepulpa.
See, a lot of people think of him as Washington because he did a lot of playing in Washington, D.C.

Yeah, I know. But he's really from Oklahoma. I guess that you could say he was one of the main, choice players that came out of Oklahoma that really can play. And I think he plays his fanny off myself.

Now, in the general area of the Southwest, everyone has always talked about a certain kind of general style that came out of there, kind of a Swing feeling, I guess, which culminated, as far as national attention, in what they call Kansas City.
But it had a whole feeling to all the bands that came out of Texas, Oklahoma, Missouri...
